item.title: The US built nearly 2,000 km of Mississippi River levees; helping erase 4,900 sq km of coastal land
item.description: The construction of levees along the Mississippi River has led to significant coastal land erosion in Louisiana by obstructing critical river sediment from reaching coastal estuaries. In an effort to combat this issue, environmental agencies are now reintroducing river mud into the affected bayous. This initiative is focused on rejuvenating the coastline and revitalizing marshland ecosystems, serving as a potential blueprint for delta restoration throughout southern Louisiana. item.title: The struggle for women to get care in Afghanistan
item.description: In this edition, French filmmaker and journalist Mélanie Nunes speaks to FRANCE 24 about her investigative report, "Afghanistan : les soignantes de l'ombre" or ‘the unsung female carers’. It follows women in the country as they try to get the heath care they need, as well as following health care providers themselves as they try to offer their services. Nunes says that the women who participated in the short-form documentary did so because “nobody cares about what they think" in their own country.
